 THIS MFA IS FILED UNDER SECTION 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 6.1.2016 PASSED IN MVC NO.2439/2015 ON THE FILE OF THE 16 TH ADDITIONAL JUDGE, MEMBER, MACT, COURT OF SMALL CAUSES, BENGALURU, PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

In this appeal, the petitioners have challenged the judgment and award dated 06.01.2016 in M.V.C.No.2439/2015 passed by the M.A.C.T., Bengaluru (SCCH-14) ('the Tribunal' for short).
2.
For the sake of convenience, the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are, on 19.04.2015 at about 10:30 am, the husband of the 1st petitioner,
father of petitioners No.2 and 3 by name Chandar, the deceased, while riding the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-01/VA-9721 along with the 1st petitioner as NC: 2023:KHC:37687 pillion rider on Palamaner-Bengaluru National Highway-4 at Gangavaram Junction, a milk tanker bearing Reg.No.KA-41/B-212 hit against the motor cycle from opposite direction killing the deceased at the spot and injuring the 1st petitioner.
The petitioners being the dependants of the deceased have filed claim petition before the Tribunal.
Claim was opposed by the respondents.
The Tribunal after taking the evidence, by impugned judgment, awarded a sum of Rs.13,93,000/- with 9% interest p.a.
Pleading inadequacy and seeking enhancement, the petitioners have filed this appeal on various grounds.

4. Heard the arguments of Sri. Gurudev Prasad. K.T, learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri. A.
Ravi Shankar, learned counsel for the Insurance Company.
5.

It is the contention of learned counsel for the petitioners that the deceased was working as a Sales Representative at M/s Light Illusions, Bengaluru and NC: 2023:KHC:37687 drawing a salary of Rs.25,000/- per month.

In spite of placing sufficient evidence, the Tribunal has assessed the Smt Sangeetha vs The Manager on 13 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82511790/
2 notional income at Rs.8,000/- and without considering the conventional heads properly, awarded lesser compensation and sought for enhancement.
6. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has contended that to support that the deceased was working as a Sales Representative and earning Rs.25,000/- salary, there is no proof.

The Tribunal has rightly assessed the notional income of Rs.8,000/- and awarded excess compensation under conventional heads and there is no need for enhancement and he supported the impugned judgment.
7. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on both sides and also perused the materials on record.

8. There is no dispute as to the accident, cause of the accident and death of the deceased on account of NC: 2023:KHC:37687 the accident, petitioners being the dependents entitled to claim compensation.
The petitioners are pleading that the deceased was working as a Sales Representative at M/s Light Illusions, Commercial Street, Bengaluru, earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
To this extent, they have relied upon the evidence of PW- 2 Sri. Mohammed Saleem and Ex.P11 to P13.

The Tribunal has considered Exs.P8 and P12 as proof of income and made a clear observation that PW-2 has not produced any attendance register, wage register, deduction of professional tax and income tax pertains to the deceased or any bank statement to show that the deceased has received any salary from PW-2.
The Tribunal has rightly recorded its reasons why it is not able to accept the evidence of PW-2 and contents of Exs.P8 and P12.
I do not find any error in the finding recorded by the Tribunal.
9. The driving licence pertains to the deceased indicates that he was born on 28.10.1974, aged 40 NC: 2023:KHC:37687 years on the date of accident.
Even if the avocation of the deceased is taken as no proof, the notional income of a person with no proof of income has to be assessed not less than Rs.9,000/- in the year 2015.
In this background, assessment of notional income at Rs.8,000/- by the Tribunal is on the lower side.

9.1. In a case of this nature, principle of assessment of compensation is settled by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co.Ltd. -vs- Pranay Sethi and Others1and Sarla Varma (Smt.) and Others -vs- Delhi Transport Corporation and

10. By applying these principles, compensation has to be assessed.
Since, the deceased was aged 40 years with no proof of income, future prospects of 25% has to be considered.
There are 3 dependents and therefore, 1/3rd has to be deducted towards personal expenses.

If all these factors are considered, the (2017) 16 SCC 680 (2009) 6 SCC 121 NC: 2023:KHC:37687 assessment of loss of dependency will be Rs.9,000/- + Rs.2,250/- (25%) = Rs.11,250/- - Rs.3,750/- (1/3rd) = Rs.7,500/- x 12 x '15' multiplier = Rs.13,50,000/-.

Under conventional heads, towards loss of consortium to wife,
loss of love and affection to children, a sum of Rs.40,000/- each has to be assessed.
Towards funeral expenses and loss of estate, Rs.15,000/- each has to be assessed.
If all these are summed up, it comes to Rs.15,00,000/- as against Rs.13,93,000/-, thereby enhancement of Rs.1,07,000/-.
This is the just compensation that the petitioners are entitled to, in the facts and circumstances of the case.

Hence, the appeal merits consideration, in the result, the following:
ORDER i) Appeal is allowed in part.
ii) Impugned judgment is modified.
iii) Petitioners are entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.1,07,000/- with interest of 6% p.a.
NC: 2023:KHC:37687 iv) The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation within eight weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of the judgment.
v) Amount in deposit, if any, shall be transmitted to the Tribunal along with records forthwith.
